learning_objective: 🎯 Master the timeline of English grammar and learn how to use verbs to talk about the past, present, and future perfectly!

main_concepts.concept_title: ⏳ What is a Tense? (The Time Machine)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Tenses act like a time machine for verbs. They change the spelling of a verb to tell the reader EXACTLY when an action happened. 'I play' means I do it every day, 'I played' means it is over, and 'I will play' means it has not happened yet!

Use the Simple Present tense for things you do every day (habits) or universal truths. Example: 'The sun RISES in the east' or 'I BRUSH my teeth daily.' Rule: Add 's' or 'es' to the verb if the subject is singular (He plays, She goes).

Whenever you see the word 'Continuous', think of an action that is in progress. You MUST use an 'ing' verb! Present Continuous: 'I am playing' (Right now). Past Continuous: 'I was playing' (In the middle of doing it yesterday).

Perfect tenses talk about completed actions that still matter. Present Perfect uses 'has/have + 3rd form of verb'. Example: 'I HAVE FINISHED my homework.' (I finished it in the past, but the result is that I am free right now!).
Use 'will' or 'shall' plus the base verb to talk about things that haven't happened yet. Example: 'It WILL RAIN tomorrow.' We use it for promises, sudden decisions, and future facts!

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The Time Travel Diary
fun_activity.instructions: Write three sentences about a pizza. One in the past (yesterday), one in the present continuous (right now), and one in the future (tomorrow). Example: I ate pizza. I am eating pizza. I will eat pizza!

quick_recap: ⭐ Tenses change the verb to show the time of an action.
⭐ Simple Present is for daily habits and universal facts.
⭐ Continuous tenses always use an 'ing' verb to show ongoing action.
⭐ Perfect tenses use has/have/had to show a completed action.
⭐ Future tense uses 'will' to talk about plans and predictions.
